references.text: Describes the burnt offering as a 'pleasing aroma to the Lord' (רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהוָה), the same expression used in Numbers 15:13
Refers to the sacrifice as 'a pleasing aroma to the Lord', parallel to the wording in Numbers 15:13
States that the same law shall apply to the native (הָאֶזְרָח) and the foreigner, corresponding to the context in Numbers 15
Confirms the principle of one law for the native and the foreigner
Elaborates on the same principle that one regulation shall apply to both the native Israelite and the foreigner
The first time the expression 'pleasing aroma' (רֵיחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ) is used regarding an offering to the Lord
Paul uses the same sacrificial terminology (ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας) concerning Christ's sacrifice as a pleasing aroma to God
